This file **adds** to the analysis of 10 October 2026 (`code/analysis.Rmd`, `output/analysis.html`); no earlier file is modified. All new outputs carry the prefix `aindex_` (tables) or `fig7`–`fig10` (figures).

# 1. The method, as defined by Benati & Capurri (2026)

Source: Stefano Benati & Agnese Capurri, "The Alignment index and its application to voting at the United Nations General Assembly", *Quality & Quantity* 60 (2026): 16075–16107, [doi:10.1007/s11135-026-02814-x](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11135-026-02814-x) (open access, CC BY 4.0).

* Votes are coded *X* = 1 (Yes), 2 (Abstain), 3 (No). **S-index** (Signorino & Ritter; Eq. 1): $s_{ij} = 1 - \frac{1}{|K_{ij}|}\sum_{k\in K_{ij}}|x_{ik}-x_{jk}|$, over the set $K_{ij}$ of votes in which both states voted; range −1 to 1.
* **Expected S under independent voting** (Eq. 4): $s^0_{ij} = 1 - 1\cdot(p_{YA}+p_{AN}+p_{AY}+p_{NA}) - 2\cdot(p_{YN}+p_{NY})$ with $p_{uv} = p_{i,u}\,p_{j,v}$ from each state's marginal vote shares (Eq. 3).
* **Alignment index** (Eq. 5): $a_{ij} = s_{ij} - s^0_{ij}$. Zero separates aligned (>0) from misaligned (<0) pairs. **Generalised index** (Eq. 15): $a^{\lambda}_{ij} = s_{ij} - \lambda s^0_{ij}$ (λ = 0 gives S, λ = 1 gives A).
* **Clique partitioning (CP)** (Eqs. 8–12): choose the partition that maximises the sum of $a_{ij}$ over all pairs placed in the same cluster, subject to transitivity; the number of clusters is not fixed and outliers emerge as singletons. The authors discard clusters of ≤ 4 states as uninformative (*k\**) and measure **cohesion** as the mean $a_{ij}$ within a cluster.
* **Absences**: main specification treats absence as missing (their M1); sensitivity check codes absence as abstention (M2).

**Implementation choices that the paper leaves open (documented here).** (i) Eq. 3 estimates marginals over all votes a state cast ($K_i$), while Table 1 and the worked example assume $K_i = K_j = K_{ij}$. Our main specification uses marginals on $K_{ij}$ ("joint"), so that A = 0 exactly when the observed joint table equals the product of its own margins; the literal Eq. 3 version ("own") is reported as a robustness check. The two differ only when absences are frequent — which they are on procedural votes. (ii) The authors' code is not public (CRAN release announced), so the CP model is solved with a documented heuristic (random restarts + Louvain-style local moving and cluster aggregation + iterated local search), validated against the exact integer programme (Eqs. 8–12, solved with `lpSolve`) in §2.

# 2. Verification of the implementation

```{r verify}
tab <- matrix(c(120,10,40, 10,10,10, 40,0,0), 3, byrow = TRUE)          # Sect. 3.2 worked example (rows r, columns c)
a <- b <- c(); for (u in 1:3) for (v in 1:3) { a <- c(a, rep(u, tab[u, v])); b <- c(b, rep(v, tab[u, v])) }
ex1 <- pair_index(a, b)
ex2 <- pair_index(c(rep(1, 80), rep(3, 20)), c(rep(1, 60), rep(3, 20), rep(1, 20)))   # Sect. 3.1 example
kable(rbind(`Worked example, Sect. 3.2 (paper: S = 0.206, S0 = 0.280, A = -0.074)` = ex1,
            `Example, Sect. 3.1 (paper: S = 0.2, A = -0.16)` = ex2) %>% round(3),
      caption = "Our functions reproduce the paper's numerical examples (differences in the third decimal are the paper's rounding of cell shares)")
# Vectorised matrix version equals pairwise version
Xt <- matrix(sample(c(1,1,1,1,2,3,NA), 300 * 10, TRUE), 300, 10)
Mt <- amatrix(Xt); err <- max(sapply(1:9, function(i) sapply((i+1):10, function(j) abs(Mt$A[i,j] - pair_index(Xt[,i], Xt[,j])["A"]))) %>% unlist())
cat("Max |matrix A - pairwise A| on simulated data:", signif(err, 3), "\n")
# Heuristic CP vs exact ILP on 30 random signed instances (n = 12-18)
val <- map_dfr(1:30, function(s) { set.seed(s); n <- sample(12:18, 1); W <- matrix(rnorm(n*n), n); W <- (W + t(W))/2; diag(W) <- 0
  dimnames(W) <- list(1:n, 1:n); ex <- cp_exact(W); h <- cp_heuristic(W, 30, 30, seed = s)
  tibble(n = n, exact = ex$objective, heuristic = h$objective, same_optimum = abs(ex$objective - h$objective) < 1e-6) })
cat("Heuristic reached the exact ILP optimum in", sum(val$same_optimum), "of", nrow(val), "random instances\n")
```

# 3. Data

```{r data}
items <- read_csv(dd("fc_vote_items_raw.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
votes <- read_csv(dd("fc_votes_long_raw.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
cls   <- read_csv(dd("procedural_classification.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
ref   <- read_csv(dd("country_reference.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
v26   <- read_csv(dd("fc2026_votes_known.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
plen  <- read_csv(dd("plenary_unvotes_2018_2019.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
items_v <- items %>% filter(valid == 1) %>% left_join(cls, by = "vote_id") %>% mutate(category = replace_na(category, "substantive"))
votes_v <- votes %>% semi_join(items_v, by = "vote_id")
members <- sort(ref$country)
make_X <- function(long, ids, m2 = FALSE) {
  X <- long %>% filter(vote_id %in% ids) %>% mutate(x = code3(vote)) %>% select(vote_id, country, x) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = country, values_from = x)
  X <- X[match(ids, X$vote_id), ]; M <- as.matrix(X[, -1, drop = FALSE]); miss <- setdiff(members, colnames(M))
  if (length(miss)) M <- cbind(M, matrix(NA, nrow(M), length(miss), dimnames = list(NULL, miss)))
  M <- M[, members, drop = FALSE]; rownames(M) <- ids; if (m2) M[is.na(M)] <- 2; M
}
ids_P18 <- items_v %>% filter(category != "substantive") %>% pull(vote_id)
ids_SUB <- items_v %>% filter(category == "substantive") %>% pull(vote_id)
v26l <- v26 %>% select(vote_id, country, vote)
X <- list(
  P18 = make_X(votes_v, ids_P18),
  P26 = rbind(make_X(votes_v, ids_P18), make_X(v26l, "FC81_CRP1")),
  SUB = make_X(votes_v, ids_SUB),
  PLEN = make_X(plen, unique(plen$vote_id)))
# Hypothetical bound for 2026: every state not named 'against'/'abstaining' coded Yes (in reality 46 of them did not vote)
x26b <- make_X(v26l, "FC81_CRP1"); x26b[is.na(x26b)] <- 1
X$P26B <- rbind(make_X(votes_v, ids_P18), x26b)
# M2 versions: absence coded as abstention
X2 <- list(P18 = make_X(votes_v, ids_P18, TRUE), SUB = make_X(votes_v, ids_SUB, TRUE), PLEN = make_X(plen, unique(plen$vote_id), TRUE))
lab_ds <- c(P18 = "FC procedural 2018–24 (18 votes)", P26 = "FC procedural 2018–26 (+ CRP.1, published positions only)",
            P26B = "FC procedural 2018–26 (+ CRP.1, unnamed states coded Yes: hypothetical bound)",
            SUB = "FC substantive 2018–23 (611 votes)", PLEN = "UNGA plenary 2018–19 (185 roll calls)")
min_n <- c(P18 = 8, P26 = 8, P26B = 8, SUB = 100, PLEN = 50)
kable(tibble(dataset = names(X), description = lab_ds[names(X)], votes = map_int(X, nrow),
             states_meeting_min = map_int(names(X), ~ sum(colSums(!is.na(X[[.x]])) >= min_n[.x])), min_votes_cast = min_n[names(X)]),
      caption = "Vote sets. Pairs are scored only when both states voted together at least `min_votes_cast` times; CP uses states that cast at least that many votes")
```

The plenary set comes from the CRAN package `unvotes` 0.3.0 (Voeten, Strezhnev & Bailey's roll-call data, which the package redistributes; it ends in December 2019 and drops absences). Raw plenary roll calls for 2020–2024 are not reachable from the box: the Harvard Dataverse handle hdl:1902.1/12379 now resolves to the *Ideal Points* dataset, which holds only dyadic agreement scores; the UN Digital Library voting data are behind a bot challenge. So the A-index can be computed for plenary votes in 2018–19 only, while the earlier Lijphart comparison used the 2018–24 dyadic scores.

# 4. Pairwise A vs. the earlier agreement scores

```{r pairs}
pairs <- tribble(~c1, ~c2,
  "China","Russian Federation", "India","Russian Federation", "China","India", "Belarus","Russian Federation",
  "Iran (Islamic Republic of)","Russian Federation", "Democratic People’s Republic of Korea","Russian Federation", "Nicaragua","Russian Federation",
  "Syrian Arab Republic","Russian Federation", "Algeria","Russian Federation", "Mali","Russian Federation", "Niger","Russian Federation",
  "Brazil","Russian Federation", "South Africa","Russian Federation", "United States of America","Russian Federation",
  "China","United States of America", "India","United States of America")
boot_ci <- function(a, b, R = 1000) { ok <- which(!is.na(a) & !is.na(b)); if (length(ok) < 3) return(c(NA, NA))
  bs <- replicate(R, { k <- sample(ok, length(ok), TRUE); pair_index(a[k], b[k])["A"] }); quantile(bs, c(.025, .975), na.rm = TRUE) }
pt <- map_dfr(c("P18","P26","SUB","PLEN"), function(ds) pmap_dfr(pairs, function(c1, c2) {
  a <- X[[ds]][, c1]; b <- X[[ds]][, c2]; j <- pair_index(a, b, "joint"); o <- pair_index(a, b, "own")
  m2 <- if (ds %in% names(X2)) pair_index(X2[[ds]][, c1], X2[[ds]][, c2])["A"] else NA
  ci <- if (j["n"] >= 3) boot_ci(a, b) else c(NA, NA)
  tibble(dataset = ds, pair = short(paste(c1, "–", c2)), n = j["n"], lijphart = j["lijphart"], S = j["S"], A = j["A"],
         A_lo = ci[1], A_hi = ci[2], A_own_marginals = o["A"], A_M2_absent_as_abstain = m2) }))
write_csv(pt, od("aindex_table_pairs.csv"))
kable(pt %>% mutate(across(lijphart:A_M2_absent_as_abstain, ~ round(., 3))), caption = "Pairwise Lijphart agreement, S-index and A-index (95% bootstrap interval over votes, 1,000 resamples) by vote set")
```

```{r rankings}
rk <- map_dfr(c("P18","P26","SUB","PLEN"), function(ds) { M <- amatrix(X[[ds]], min_n = min_n[ds]); a <- M$A["Russian Federation", ]
  L <- sapply(members, function(cn) pair_index(X[[ds]][, "Russian Federation"], X[[ds]][, cn])["lijphart"]); L[M$n["Russian Federation", ] < min_n[ds]] <- NA
  tibble(dataset = ds, country = members, A = a, lijphart = L) %>% filter(country != "Russian Federation", !is.na(A)) %>%
    mutate(rank_A = rank(-A, ties.method = "min"), rank_lijphart = rank(-lijphart, ties.method = "min"), partners = n()) })
write_csv(rk, od("aindex_table_partners_of_russia.csv"))
kable(rk %>% filter(country %in% c("China","India","Belarus","Iran (Islamic Republic of)","Democratic People’s Republic of Korea","Nicaragua","Syrian Arab Republic","Algeria","Mali","Niger","Burkina Faso","United States of America")) %>%
        mutate(country = short(country), across(c(A, lijphart), ~ round(., 3))) %>% arrange(dataset, rank_A),
      caption = "Where selected states rank among Russia's partners (1 = most aligned with Russia)")
pct_pairs <- map_dfr(c("P18","SUB","PLEN"), function(ds) { M <- amatrix(X[[ds]], min_n = min_n[ds])$A; v <- M[upper.tri(M)]; v <- v[!is.na(v)]
  tibble(dataset = ds, pairs_scored = length(v), share_A_positive = mean(v > 0), median_A = median(v),
         China_Russia_A = M["China","Russian Federation"], China_Russia_percentile = mean(v < M["China","Russian Federation"])) })
kable(pct_pairs %>% mutate(across(-c(dataset, pairs_scored), ~ round(., 3))), caption = "Distribution of A across all scored pairs")
```

```{r fig7, fig.height=7}
f7 <- pt %>% filter(dataset %in% c("P18","SUB","PLEN")) %>% select(dataset, pair, `Lijphart agreement (earlier)` = lijphart, `A-index (Benati & Capurri)` = A, A_lo, A_hi) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(`Lijphart agreement (earlier)`, `A-index (Benati & Capurri)`), names_to = "measure", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(A_lo = if_else(measure == "A-index (Benati & Capurri)", A_lo, NA_real_), A_hi = if_else(measure == "A-index (Benati & Capurri)", A_hi, NA_real_),
         dataset = factor(lab_ds[dataset], levels = lab_ds[c("P18","SUB","PLEN")]),
         pair = factor(pair, levels = rev(unique(pt$pair))))
g7 <- ggplot(f7, aes(x = value, y = pair, colour = measure, shape = measure)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey40", linewidth = .4) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = A_lo, xmax = A_hi), height = 0, alpha = .5, na.rm = TRUE) + geom_point(size = 2.6, na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~ dataset, nrow = 1) + scale_colour_manual(values = c("#7a0177", "grey55")) + scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-1, 1)) +
  labs(title = "Figure 7. Raw agreement versus chance-corrected alignment (A-index), selected pairs",
       subtitle = "A = observed similarity minus similarity expected under independent voting; 0 separates aligned from misaligned pairs.\nLines: 95% bootstrap intervals for A (resampling votes). Pairs with too few joint votes are omitted.",
       x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL, shape = NULL,
       caption = "Sources: A/C.1/73–79/PV.x (validated recorded votes); Voeten et al. roll calls via R package unvotes 0.3.0; method: Benati & Capurri (2026), doi:10.1007/s11135-026-02814-x.") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text = element_text(size = 9))
ggsave(fd("fig7_aindex_vs_agreement.png"), g7, width = 12.5, height = 7.2, dpi = 200); g7
```

# 5. Does China's 2026 abstention still look like a departure?

```{r china2026}
cr <- function(ds, m = "joint") pair_index(X[[ds]][, "China"], X[[ds]][, "Russian Federation"], m)
ctab <- map_dfr(c("P18","P26","P26B"), ~ tibble(dataset = .x, description = lab_ds[.x], !!!as.list(cr(.x)), A_own = cr(.x, "own")["A"]))
kable(ctab %>% mutate(across(c(lijphart, S, S0, A, A_own), ~ round(., 3))), caption = "China–Russia on procedural votes, before and after adding the 2026 programme-of-work vote")
write_csv(ctab, od("aindex_table_china_russia_2026.csv"))
# Same decomposition for Russia's other 2026 'No' partners and for China's other partners
dec <- map_dfr(c("Iran (Islamic Republic of)","Democratic People’s Republic of Korea","Nicaragua","China","India","Algeria","Mali","Niger"), function(cn)
  map_dfr(c("P18","P26"), ~ tibble(country = short(cn), dataset = .x, !!!as.list(pair_index(X[[.x]][, cn], X[[.x]][, "Russian Federation"])))))
kable(dec %>% mutate(across(c(lijphart, S, S0, A), ~ round(., 3))) %>% select(country, dataset, n, lijphart, S, S0, A),
      caption = "A with Russia before (P18) and after (P26) the 2026 vote, for the states whose 2026 positions are published")
rk26 <- rk %>% filter(dataset %in% c("P18","P26"), country %in% c("China","Iran (Islamic Republic of)","Democratic People’s Republic of Korea","Nicaragua","Belarus","Cuba","Syrian Arab Republic","Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of)","India","Algeria","Mali","Niger")) %>%
  select(dataset, country, A, rank_A, partners) %>% mutate(country = short(country), A = round(A, 3)) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = dataset, values_from = c(A, rank_A, partners))
kable(rk26, caption = "Rank among Russia's procedural partners before and after the 2026 vote (1 = most aligned)")
jt <- table(China = factor(X$P18[, "China"], 1:3, c("Yes","Abstain","No")), Russia = factor(X$P18[, "Russian Federation"], 1:3, c("Yes","Abstain","No")), useNA = "ifany")
kable(as.data.frame.matrix(jt), caption = "China (rows) × Russia (columns), 18 procedural votes 2018–24")
# Bootstrap: is the post-2026 value outside the baseline's sampling range?
a <- X$P18[, "China"]; b <- X$P18[, "Russian Federation"]
bs <- replicate(4000, { k <- sample(18, 18, TRUE); pair_index(a[k], b[k])["A"] })
cat("Baseline A (2018–24):", round(cr("P18")["A"], 3), "| bootstrap 95% interval:", round(quantile(bs, .025, na.rm = TRUE), 3), "to", round(quantile(bs, .975, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    "| after adding CRP.1:", round(cr("P26")["A"], 3), "\n")
# Expectation under China's own baseline: if China and Russia vote independently with their 2018-24 marginals,
# P(China votes differently from Russia's 'No')
pc <- marg(a[!is.na(a)]); cat("China's 2018–24 procedural marginals (Yes/Abst/No):", round(pc, 3), "-> P(not No | independence) =", round(1 - pc[3], 3), "\n")
# Predictive check: Russia's closest procedural partners (A, 2018–24) and their 2026 programme-of-work vote
pred <- rk %>% filter(dataset == "P18") %>% arrange(rank_A) %>% slice_head(n = 15) %>%
  left_join(v26 %>% select(country, vote_2026 = vote), by = "country") %>% mutate(vote_2026 = replace_na(vote_2026, "Yes or not voting (unpublished)"), country = short(country))
kable(pred %>% select(rank_A, country, A, lijphart, vote_2026) %>% mutate(across(c(A, lijphart), ~ round(., 3))),
      caption = "Russia's 15 most aligned partners on procedural votes 2018–24 (A-index) and how they voted on CRP.1 in 2026")
write_csv(pred, od("aindex_table_russia_partners_vs_2026.csv"))
# Substantive benchmark: China–Russia A by year
yr <- items_v %>% filter(category == "substantive") %>% select(vote_id, year)
by_year <- map_dfr(sort(unique(yr$year)), function(y) { ids <- yr$vote_id[yr$year == y]; Xs <- X$SUB[ids, , drop = FALSE]
  bind_rows(tibble(year = y, pair = "China–Russia", !!!as.list(pair_index(Xs[, "China"], Xs[, "Russian Federation"]))),
            tibble(year = y, pair = "India–Russia", !!!as.list(pair_index(Xs[, "India"], Xs[, "Russian Federation"])))) })
kable(by_year %>% mutate(across(c(lijphart, S, S0, A), ~ round(., 3))), caption = "Substantive First Committee votes: A by year")
write_csv(by_year, od("aindex_table_substantive_by_year.csv"))
```

# 6. Clique partitioning: blocs in the A-index network

```{r cp}
run_cp <- function(ds, lambda = 1, restarts = 60, ils = 40, M2 = FALSE) {
  Xd <- if (M2) X2[[ds]] else X[[ds]]
  keep <- colSums(!is.na(Xd)) >= min_n[ds]; M <- amatrix(Xd[, keep], lambda = lambda, min_n = min_n[ds])
  W <- M$A; W[is.na(W)] <- 0; h <- cp_heuristic(W, restarts, ils)
  list(labels = h$labels, W = W, A = M$A, objective = h$objective, share_best = h$share_best, all = h$all, objs = h$objs)
}
cps <- list(P18 = run_cp("P18"), P26 = run_cp("P26"), SUB = run_cp("SUB"), PLEN = run_cp("PLEN"))
cps_m2 <- list(P18 = run_cp("P18", M2 = TRUE), SUB = run_cp("SUB", M2 = TRUE), PLEN = run_cp("PLEN", M2 = TRUE))
describe_cp <- function(cp, ds) { lab <- cp$labels; sz <- table(lab); big <- names(sz)[sz >= 5]
  name_of <- function(l) { m <- names(lab)[lab == l]
    if ("United States of America" %in% m) "Cluster with USA" else if ("Russian Federation" %in% m) "Cluster with Russia" else if ("China" %in% m) "Cluster with China" else paste0("Other cluster ", l) }
  coh <- function(m) { w <- cp$A[m, m]; mean(w[upper.tri(w)], na.rm = TRUE) }
  tibble(dataset = ds, cluster = map_chr(big, name_of), size = as.integer(sz[big]), cohesion_meanA = map_dbl(big, ~ coh(names(lab)[lab == .x])),
         members = map_chr(big, ~ paste(short(sort(names(lab)[lab == .x])), collapse = ", "))) %>%
    bind_rows(tibble(dataset = ds, cluster = "Singletons / clusters of ≤4 (outliers)", size = sum(sz[sz < 5]), cohesion_meanA = NA,
                     members = paste(short(sort(names(lab)[lab %in% names(sz)[sz < 5]])), collapse = ", "))) }
cpt <- imap_dfr(cps, describe_cp)
write_csv(cpt, od("aindex_table_cp_clusters.csv"))
kable(cpt %>% mutate(cohesion_meanA = round(cohesion_meanA, 3)), caption = "Clique-partitioning blocs (λ = 1, absence = missing). k* counts clusters of ≥ 5 states")
kable(tibble(dataset = names(cps), states = map_int(cps, ~ length(.x$labels)), k_raw = map_int(cps, ~ max(.x$labels)),
             k_star = map_int(cps, ~ sum(table(.x$labels) >= 5)), objective = map_dbl(cps, "objective"), share_restarts_at_best = map_dbl(cps, "share_best"),
             ARI_vs_M2 = c(ari(cps$P18$labels, cps_m2$P18$labels[names(cps$P18$labels)]), NA,
                           ari(cps$SUB$labels, cps_m2$SUB$labels[names(cps$SUB$labels)]), ari(cps$PLEN$labels, cps_m2$PLEN$labels[names(cps$PLEN$labels)]))) %>%
        mutate(across(c(objective, share_restarts_at_best, ARI_vs_M2), ~ round(., 3))),
      caption = "Partition summary; ARI_vs_M2 compares with absence-as-abstention (M2) on the states common to both")
# Who sits with whom across vote sets
keyc <- c("Russian Federation","China","India","Belarus","Iran (Islamic Republic of)","Democratic People’s Republic of Korea","Nicaragua","Syrian Arab Republic","Cuba",
          "Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of)","Algeria","Mali","Niger","Burkina Faso","Egypt","Brazil","South Africa","United States of America","France","Germany")
same_as <- function(cp, x, y) if (all(c(x, y) %in% names(cp$labels))) cp$labels[x] == cp$labels[y] else NA
memb <- map_dfr(names(cps), function(ds) tibble(dataset = ds, country = short(keyc),
  in_cp = keyc %in% names(cps[[ds]]$labels), with_Russia = map_lgl(keyc, ~ same_as(cps[[ds]], .x, "Russian Federation")),
  with_USA = map_lgl(keyc, ~ same_as(cps[[ds]], .x, "United States of America")),
  cluster_size = map_int(keyc, ~ if (.x %in% names(cps[[ds]]$labels)) sum(cps[[ds]]$labels == cps[[ds]]$labels[.x]) else NA_integer_)))
kable(memb %>% pivot_wider(names_from = dataset, values_from = c(in_cp, with_Russia, cluster_size), names_vary = "slowest") %>% select(-starts_with("with_USA")),
      caption = "Key states: placed in the partition? in Russia's cluster? size of own cluster")
```

## 6.1 Bridging or peripheral? China's position in the A-network

Definitions (descriptive, not from the paper): *within-cluster alignment* = mean A with the other members of one's CP cluster; *strength* = sum of positive A; *participation coefficient* $P_i = 1 - \sum_c (w^+_{ic}/w^+_i)^2$ over the large clusters (0 = all positive alignment inside one cluster; higher = alignment spread across clusters, i.e. bridging); *betweenness* (normalised) on the graph of edges with A > 0.02, edge length 1/A. A state is read as **bridging** if it has high participation and betweenness, and as **peripheral** if its positive ties are weak and it sits at the edge of its own cluster.

```{r position}
position <- function(cp, ds) {
  W <- cp$A; W[is.na(W)] <- 0; lab <- cp$labels; sz <- table(lab); big <- names(sz)[sz >= 5]; nm <- names(lab)
  Wp <- pmax(W, 0); s <- rowSums(Wp)
  wc <- sapply(big, function(cl) rowSums(Wp[, nm[lab == cl], drop = FALSE])); if (is.null(dim(wc))) wc <- matrix(wc, ncol = 1)
  Pc <- 1 - rowSums((wc / pmax(rowSums(wc), 1e-12))^2)
  within <- sapply(nm, function(i) { m <- setdiff(nm[lab == lab[i]], i); if (length(m)) mean(W[i, m]) else NA })
  Wb <- W * (W > 0.02)   # edges: A > 0.02 (avoids near-zero weights producing numerically meaningless path lengths)
  g <- graph_from_adjacency_matrix(Wb, mode = "undirected", weighted = TRUE, diag = FALSE)
  btw <- betweenness(g, weights = 1 / E(g)$weight, normalized = TRUE)
  tibble(dataset = ds, country = nm, cluster_size = as.integer(sz[as.character(lab)]), strength = s, within_cluster_A = within,
         participation = Pc, betweenness = btw[nm]) %>%
    mutate(across(c(strength, within_cluster_A, participation, betweenness), ~ percent_rank(.), .names = "{.col}_pctile"))
}
pos <- imap_dfr(cps, position)
write_csv(pos, od("aindex_table_node_positions.csv"))
kable(pos %>% filter(country %in% c("China","India","Russian Federation","Iran (Islamic Republic of)","Belarus","Algeria","Brazil","South Africa","Egypt","United States of America")) %>%
        mutate(country = short(country), across(c(strength:betweenness_pctile), ~ round(., 3))) %>% arrange(dataset, desc(betweenness)),
      caption = "Network position (percentiles are among all states in that partition)")
```

```{r network_fig, fig.height=8}
net_plot <- function(cp, ds, title, file, top = 4, seed = 7) {
  W <- cp$A; W[is.na(W)] <- 0; nm <- rownames(W); lab <- cp$labels[nm]; sz <- table(lab)
  # keep, for each state, its `top` strongest positive ties (readability); layout uses these edges
  keep <- matrix(FALSE, nrow(W), ncol(W)); for (i in seq_along(nm)) { o <- order(-W[i, ]); o <- o[W[i, o] > 0][seq_len(min(top, sum(W[i, ] > 0)))]; keep[i, o] <- TRUE }
  keep <- keep | t(keep); Wk <- W * keep; Wk[Wk < 0] <- 0
  g <- graph_from_adjacency_matrix(Wk, mode = "undirected", weighted = TRUE, diag = FALSE)
  # draw states in CP clusters of >= 5 that belong to the largest connected component; outliers are listed instead
  comp <- components(g); gc <- which(comp$membership == which.max(comp$csize) & as.integer(sz[as.character(lab)]) >= 5)
  dropped <- setdiff(nm, nm[gc]); g <- induced_subgraph(g, gc); nm <- nm[gc]; lab <- lab[nm]
  wl <- E(g)$weight; wl <- 0.2 + 0.8 * (wl - min(wl)) / max(1e-9, max(wl) - min(wl))   # rescaled weights for layout only
  set.seed(seed); L <- layout_with_fr(g, weights = wl, niter = 3000)
  nodes <- tibble(country = nm, x = L[,1], y = L[,2], cl = as.character(lab), size = as.integer(sz[as.character(lab)])) %>%
    mutate(cluster = case_when(size < 5 ~ "Outlier (cluster ≤ 4)",
                               cl == lab["United States of America"] ~ "CP cluster containing USA",
                               cl == lab["Russian Federation"] ~ "CP cluster containing Russia",
                               TRUE ~ paste("Other CP cluster", cl)))
  el <- as_edgelist(g, names = FALSE); edges <- tibble(x = L[el[,1],1], y = L[el[,1],2], xend = L[el[,2],1], yend = L[el[,2],2], w = E(g)$weight)
  labs_show <- c("Russian Federation","China","India","United States of America","Iran (Islamic Republic of)","Belarus","Democratic People’s Republic of Korea","Nicaragua",
                 "Syrian Arab Republic","Cuba","Algeria","Mali","Niger","Egypt","Brazil","South Africa","France","Germany","Japan","Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of)","Indonesia","Pakistan","Israel")
  cols <- c("CP cluster containing USA" = "#2b8cbe", "CP cluster containing Russia" = "#d7301f", "Outlier (cluster ≤ 4)" = "grey60")
  others <- setdiff(unique(nodes$cluster), names(cols)); cols <- c(cols, setNames(c("#fdae61","#4daf4a","#984ea3","#a65628")[seq_along(others)], others))
  gg <- ggplot() + geom_segment(data = edges, aes(x, y, xend = xend, yend = yend, alpha = w), colour = "grey50", linewidth = .25) +
    geom_point(data = nodes, aes(x, y, colour = cluster), size = 2.2) +
    geom_point(data = nodes %>% filter(country == "China"), aes(x, y), shape = 21, size = 5, stroke = 1.2, colour = "black") +
    geom_text(data = nodes %>% filter(country %in% labs_show), aes(x, y, label = short(country)), size = 3, family = "serif", vjust = -0.9) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = cols) + scale_alpha(range = c(.05, .6), guide = "none") +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = paste0("Nodes coloured by clique-partitioning cluster (λ = 1). Edges: each state's ", top, " strongest positive A ties. China circled.",
                                        if (length(dropped)) paste0("\nNot drawn (CP outliers or no positive tie to the main component): ", paste(short(dropped), collapse = ", ")) else ""),
         colour = NULL, caption = "Method: Benati & Capurri (2026), doi:10.1007/s11135-026-02814-x; CP solved heuristically (validated against exact ILP). Layout: Fruchterman–Reingold.") +
    theme_void(base_family = "serif") + theme(legend.position = "bottom", plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
  ggsave(fd(file), gg, width = 11, height = 8.5, dpi = 200); gg
}
net_plot(cps$P26, "P26", "Figure 8. A-index network, First Committee procedural votes 2018–2026", "fig8_aindex_network_procedural.png")
net_plot(cps$SUB, "SUB", "Figure 9. A-index network, First Committee substantive votes 2018–2023", "fig9_aindex_network_substantive.png")
```

## 6.2 Sensitivity to the resolution parameter λ (Eq. 15)

```{r lambda}
lams <- c(0, .5, .8, .95, 1, 1.1, 1.3, 1.6, 2)
lam <- map_dfr(c("P26","SUB","PLEN"), function(ds) map_dfr(lams, function(l) { cp <- run_cp(ds, lambda = l, restarts = 25, ils = 20); lab <- cp$labels
  tibble(dataset = ds, lambda = l, k_star = sum(table(lab) >= 5), largest = max(table(lab)),
         China_with_Russia = lab["China"] == lab["Russian Federation"], India_with_Russia = lab["India"] == lab["Russian Federation"],
         China_with_USA = lab["China"] == lab["United States of America"], India_with_USA = lab["India"] == lab["United States of America"],
         China_cluster_size = sum(lab == lab["China"])) }))
write_csv(lam, od("aindex_table_lambda_sensitivity.csv"))
kable(lam, caption = "Clique partitioning for λ from 0 (S-index) to 2")
g10 <- lam %>% select(dataset, lambda, China_with_Russia, India_with_Russia) %>% pivot_longer(-c(dataset, lambda)) %>%
  mutate(name = recode(name, China_with_Russia = "China in Russia's cluster", India_with_Russia = "India in Russia's cluster"),
         dataset = factor(lab_ds[dataset], levels = lab_ds[c("P26","SUB","PLEN")])) %>%
  mutate(y = as.integer(value) + if_else(name == "China in Russia's cluster", 0.04, -0.04)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(lambda, y, colour = name)) + geom_step(linewidth = 1, direction = "mid") + geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ dataset, ncol = 1) + scale_y_continuous(breaks = 0:1, labels = c("no","yes")) + scale_colour_manual(values = c("#7a0177", "#fdae61")) +
  labs(title = "Figure 10. Is China (or India) clustered with Russia? Sensitivity to the resolution parameter λ",
       subtitle = "λ = 0: S-index (raw similarity); λ = 1: A-index; λ > 1: stronger correction for expected similarity",
       x = "λ", y = NULL, colour = NULL, caption = "Clique partitioning on a^λ = S − λ·S0 (Benati & Capurri 2026, Eq. 15).") + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
ggsave(fd("fig10_lambda_sensitivity.png"), g10, width = 10, height = 7, dpi = 200); g10
```

# 7. Blocs: cohesion and alignment with Russia under A

```{r blocs}
grp <- list(`EU-27` = ref$country[ref$eu27 == 1], NAM = ref$country[ref$nam_2026 == 1], AES = ref$country[ref$aes_sahel == 1],
            `African Group` = ref$country[ref$un_regional_group == "African Group"], `Asia-Pacific Group` = ref$country[ref$un_regional_group == "Asia and the Pacific Group"],
            GRULAC = ref$country[str_detect(ref$un_regional_group, "GRULAC")])
bl <- map_dfr(c("P18","SUB","PLEN"), function(ds) { M <- amatrix(X[[ds]], min_n = min_n[ds])$A
  imap_dfr(grp, function(m, g) { m <- setdiff(m, "Russian Federation"); w <- M[m, m]
    tibble(dataset = ds, bloc = g, members_scored = sum(!is.na(M[m, "Russian Federation"])), cohesion_meanA = mean(w[upper.tri(w)], na.rm = TRUE),
           meanA_with_Russia = mean(M[m, "Russian Federation"], na.rm = TRUE), meanA_with_USA = mean(M[setdiff(m, "United States of America"), "United States of America"], na.rm = TRUE)) }) })
write_csv(bl, od("aindex_table_blocs.csv"))
kable(bl %>% mutate(across(c(cohesion_meanA, meanA_with_Russia, meanA_with_USA), ~ round(., 3))), caption = "Bloc cohesion (mean within-bloc A, as in the paper) and mean A with Russia and with the USA")
```

# 8. Limitations of this update

* **Small N on procedure.** A on 18–19 procedural votes is noisy; bootstrap intervals (§4) are wide, and one added vote cannot move A outside them. The 2026 vote enters only for pairs among the 12 states whose positions were published; the "coded Yes" variant is a hypothetical bound, not data.
* **Missing marginals.** Many states rarely vote on procedural motions; under M1 their pairs are not scored (minimum 8 joint votes), and states such as Burkina Faso drop out of the procedural network entirely. M2 (absence = abstention) changes this; see the ARI.
* **Implementation choices.** Marginals on $K_{ij}$ (main) vs $K_i$ (literal Eq. 3); heuristic CP (validated, but not a proof of optimality for 190 states); network-position measures are our descriptive additions, not part of the paper.
* **Plenary coverage** stops in 2019 for raw roll calls (see §3).
* **Interpretation.** A measures conditional co-voting beyond chance. It is still not coordination and not causation; abstentions remain ambiguous signals.
